items.title: Adequate modules on an affine scheme are equivalent to adequate functors
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file adequate.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For an affine scheme S = Spec(A), the lemma asserts that the category of adequate O-modules on (Sch/S)_tau is equivalent to the category of adequate module-valued functors on Alg_A (statement lines 1737-1742). The proof constructs both directions: from an adequate module F one takes the associated functor, adequate by the locality lemma; from an adequate functor F one chooses a presentation, forms the O-module defined as the kernel of the associated maps M^a -> N^a of quasi-coherent modules, and checks that its associated functor is the original F, so the module is adequate by definition (proof lines 1744-1753). The author then states that the verification that the two constructions are mutually inverse equivalences is omitted; that verification is the routine functoriality check for two explicitly displayed constructions which the span supplies (proof line 1754). The level is H3: the two constructions are written out and the omitted step is a named routine check rather than a load-bearing argument.
